rulings.decision: D as the floor, filesystem and egress containment together, applied WHEN ALL THREE of private data, untrusted content and outbound communication are present in one run. Two of the three is normal operation and is permitted: an agent reading the operator's own files and calling a model provider has private data and egress but no untrusted content, and nothing here restricts it. The rule binds on the third leg, content the run did not author. In PatterStage today that means Deep Research and any future surface that fetches the open web, where the fetched page is untrusted content arriving beside file access and an outbound channel. In-band detection runs in parallel as a tripwire and is never counted as the boundary, because a model asked to spot its own manipulation is not a control.
rulings.reason: PatterStage runs agent sessions with tool access and ships an app that dispatches inference over content it did not author. RE-RULED by the operator 2026-08-23 (session S-0004): the original draft read as forbidding the coexistence of the three legs without saying that two of them together is ordinary and safe, which would have read as a prohibition on normal Hermes use. The softening is a clarification of scope, not a lowering of the floor: containment is still the boundary for a genuine three-leg run, and the operator's instruction was to soften the rule so it does not constrain how he actually uses Hermes. What it costs: a web-fetching research run must be contained rather than trusted, which is the capability loss taken knowingly. ACCEPTED by Daniel Parke (operator), 2026-08-23, session S-0004.

rulings.decision: B and C together: a staged pre-commit secret scan and a push-path scan, with the credential files and secret environment variables named explicitly in the deny list rather than left to the scanner's defaults. ACCEPTED by Daniel Parke (operator), 2026-08-23, session S-0004.
